title: Hederasaponin C inhibits LPS-induced acute kidney injury in mice by targeting TLR4 and regulating the PIP2/NF-kappaB/NLRP3 signaling pathway.
authors: Han, Shan; Li, Siyuan; Li, Jilang; He, Jia; Wang, Qin-Qin; Gao, Xiang; Yang, Shilin; Li, Jingjing; Yuan, Renyikun; Zhong, Guoyue; Gao, Hongwei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物Hederasaponin C通过靶向TLR4调节信号通路抑制LPS诱导的急性肾损伤，属于药物药理学与炎症机制研究，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common clinical condition associated with increased incidence and mortality rates. Hederasaponin C (HSC) is one of the main active components of Pulsatilla chinensis (Bunge) Regel. HSC possesses various pharmacological activities, including anti-inflammatory activity. However, the protective effect of HSC against lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced AKI in mice remains unclear. Therefore, we investigated the protective effect of HSC against LPS-induced renal inflammation and the underlying molecular mechanisms. Herein, using MTT and LDH assays to assess both cell viability and LDH activity; using dual staining techniques to identify different cell death patterns; conducting immunoblotting, QRT-PCR, and immunofluorescence analyses to evaluate levels of protein and mRNA expression; employing immunoblotting, molecular docking, SPR experiments, and CETSA to investigate the interaction between HSC and TLR4; and studying the anti-inflammatory effects of HSC in the LPS-induced AKI. The results indicate that HSC inhibits the expression of TLR4 and the activation of NF-kappaB and PIP2 signaling pathways, while simultaneously suppressing the activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome. In animal models, HSC ameliorated LPS-induced AKI and diminished inflammatory response and the level of renal injury markers. These findings suggest that HSC has potential as a therapeutic agent to mitigate sepsis-related AKI.
abstract_zh: 急性肾损伤（AKI）是一种常见的临床病症，与发病率和死亡率增加相关。Hederasaponin C（HSC）是白头翁（Pulsatilla chinensis (Bunge) Regel）的主要活性成分之一。HSC具有多种药理活性，包括抗炎活性。然而，HSC对脂多糖（LPS）诱导的小鼠AKI的保护作用尚不清楚。因此，我们研究了HSC对LPS诱导的肾脏炎症的保护作用及其潜在的分子机制。在此，使用MTT和LDH实验评估细胞活力和LDH活性；使用双重染色技术识别不同的细胞死亡模式；进行免疫印迹、QRT-PCR和免疫荧光分析以评估蛋白质和mRNA表达水平；采用免疫印迹、分子对接、SPR实验和CETSA研究HSC与TLR4之间的相互作用；并研究HSC在LPS诱导的AKI中的抗炎作用。结果表明，HSC抑制TLR4的表达以及NF-kappaB和PIP2信号通路的激活，同时抑制NLRP3炎症小体的激活。在动物模型中，HSC改善了LPS诱导的AKI，并减轻了炎症反应和肾损伤标志物的水平。这些发现表明，HSC具有作为缓解脓毒症相关AKI的治疗剂的潜力。
